body:
## Reproduction
At 1920×1080 with `?renderer=oblique`, create and save a prison, pause, hold the right mouse button over the world canvas, activate Load by keyboard while the button remains down, then move the pointer.

## Actual
The replacement prison's minimap viewport changes from `left: 2.38975%; top: 2.38975%; width: 95.2205%; height: 95.2205%` to `left: 7.28741%; top: 8.60236%; width: 81.4966%; height: 85.4787%`. The camera turn begun in the outgoing session remains active after Load. The same scene also retains held keyboard codes and build/room/object pointer gestures; those paths need the same boundary reset.

## Expected
Changing prison sessions ends transient camera and placement input. No stale pointer movement/up should rotate the new prison or submit the old gesture into it. No camera pose save field is needed.

## Evidence
`tests/browser/oblique-camera-load-gesture.spec.ts` failed on production before the fix: one worker, 6.8 s test, 1920×1080. The test uses real Save and Load buttons, not a scene harness.

comments.body: Additional independent Full HD verification: `tests/browser/oblique-build-load-gesture.spec.ts` starts a real full-square Brick wall drag, activates Load by keyboard while left mouse remains held, then releases the pointer. With only `worldScene.releaseSessionInput()` omitted from production, the outgoing drag submitted two `PlaceBuildOrder` messages into the loaded worker (7.2 s test, red). Restored callback submitted zero orders (11.5 s suite, green). This confirms the Build path separately from the RMB camera turn. Durable evidence is in `docs/research/2026-10-02-oblique-load-gesture/README.md` on branch `codex/oblique-load-session-lifecycle-20261002`.

title: Held camera turn crosses oblique prison Load boundary
